title: Policy engine: add priority classes, per-route budgets, and deterministic decision logging
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
We need explicit, tier-aware priority evaluation in the policy engine to support hot-route capacity protection.

This ticket extends the policy engine schema + evaluation engine to:
1) Assign a deterministic priority class to every request (enterprise vs best-effort vs internal/system).
2) Evaluate per-route / per-route-group budgets and quota windows that can be consumed by routing/admission control.
3) Emit deterministic decision logs that are explainable for enterprise escalations and auditable post-incident, without adding high-cardinality overhead to the data plane.

Context
- This work is the contract that Gateway + Routing will call on the request path (or via a cached lookup) to decide admission behavior under pressure.
- Requirements from project doc: deterministic and auditable decisions; low overhead; reversible rollout; consistent semantics.

Proposed model (schema additions)
- Route identity
  - route_id: canonical string (e.g., "v1.chat.completions", "v1.embeddings", "v1.rerank")
  - route_group: optional grouping for shared defaults (e.g., "chat", "embed", "rerank")
- Priority
  - priority_class: enum
    - P0_INTERNAL (scheduler/control-plane health)
    - P1_ENTERPRISE (SLA-bound)
    - P2_STANDARD (paid/self-serve)
    - P3_BEST_EFFORT (free/trial/low-SLA)
  - priority_reason: short code describing which rule matched (e.g., "account_tier", "contract_override", "route_protected_default")
- Budgets
  - per-route budgets by tier/priority (e.g., max admitted rps, concurrency tokens, or abstract "admission units")
  - windows: fixed windows only for MVP (e.g., 1s / 10s / 1m); no sliding windows in v1
  - burst behavior: explicit burst_multiplier and burst_window for enterprise exceptions, but with hard caps

Decision outputs (contract)
- decision: ALLOW | THROTTLE | SHED | FALLBACK_ALLOWED (NOTE: actual shedding happens downstream; policy engine returns intent + reason)
- retry_after_ms: optional (set for THROTTLE, absent for SHED)
- reason_code: stable reason codes for support/customer comms
  - QUOTA_EXCEEDED
  - ROUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
  - PRIORITY_PREEMPTED
  - OVERLOAD_GUARDRAIL
  - POLICY_INVALID (should be rare; treated as fail-open for enterprise, fail-closed for best-effort—see Safety)
- annotations: key/value *limited set* for internal use (must be bounded + non-customer identifying)

Deterministic decision logging
- Each evaluation should produce a deterministic log record with:
  - decision_id: stable UUID generated from (request_id + policy_version + route_id) (exact scheme in implementation doc)
  - policy_version: monotonically increasing config version / git sha
  - input_fingerprint: hash of normalized inputs (account_id, tier, route_id, region, model_family, etc.)
  - matched_rules: ordered list of rule IDs (bounded)
  - output: decision + reason_code + priority_class + retry_after_ms
  - timing: evaluation_latency_us
- Logging requirements:
  - Do not log raw prompts, tokens, or customer payload
  - Do not add unbounded tags/labels (avoid account_id in metrics labels)
  - Logs must be queryable by request_id / decision_id for on-call debugging

Safety + failure modes
- Policy evaluation errors:
  - Enterprise (P1): fail-open to ALLOW with reason_code=POLICY_INVALID, and emit error log + metric.
  - Best-effort (P3): fail-closed to THROTTLE with a small retry_after_ms (to protect fleet).
  - All behavior must be behind feature flag (see ENG-4928)
- Stale policy cache:
  - Cache TTL max 60s; on version mismatch, refresh in background; do not block request path.

Performance constraints
- Target p99 policy eval latency <= 2ms (in-process) and <= 5ms (over RPC) in canary.
- Avoid per-request complex rule scans:
  - Pre-compile policy rules into a lookup table by (route_id, account_tier, region) where possible.
  - Ensure rule engine is deterministic: stable sorting, no time-dependent randomness.

Deliverables
- Schema changes in policy engine config (validated + backwards compatible).
- Evaluator changes returning priority_class + budgets + reason codes.
- Deterministic decision log record + sampling strategy (sample best-effort, always log enterprise decisions when THROTTLE/SHED).
- Validation tooling:
  - policy lint: duplicate/conflicting rules, missing defaults per protected route group.
  - offline "explain" command for a given (account_tier, route_id, region) combination.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Config supports priority classes + per-route budgets with safe defaults.
- [x] Same normalized inputs + same policy version produce identical outputs (byte-for-byte) across repeated evaluations.
- [x] Decision logging enabled and usable for support escalations: can answer "why did we 429?" with a stable reason_code + matched rule.
- [x] Performance target met in canary with logging on (enterprise error cases at 100%).
- [x] Security review completed (no sensitive data in logs; access-controlled log queries).

Links
- Confluence ADR: architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hot-route-capacity-protection-enforcement-points
- Design: eng-platform/systems-and-services/hot-route-capacity-protection-technical-design
- Related PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/27418

Notes
- This ticket intentionally does NOT implement routing admission control logic; routing consumes the priority_class + budgets and applies capacity signals (ENG-4924).
- Gateway enforces final 429 shape/headers; policy engine only returns stable reason_code + retry_after_ms (ENG-4922 + PR-27441).
comments: 2025-12-03 (Jordan Lee): Drafted schema extension proposal. Key open question: do we express budgets in RPS or "admission units"? Leaning admission units to keep runtime-independent; routing can translate using capacity signals. Will confirm with Mina + Ethan.

2025-12-05 (Mina Haddad): +1 on abstract admission units; keep evaluator independent of runtime shape. Routing needs: priority_class, budget ceiling, and whether fallback is permitted for this route group. Please ensure outputs are deterministic and stable for caching.

2025-12-06 (Ethan Park): Please include explicit fail-open/fail-closed semantics by tier to avoid accidental enterprise throttling during policy rollout. Also need an offline "explain" mode for on-call.

2025-12-09 (Allison Grant): Logging format looks good. Please ensure we do NOT introduce high-cardinality metrics tags (account_id, request_id). Logs are fine; metrics must be aggregated by route_id/priority_class/region only.

2025-12-10 (Amara Diallo): For gateway 429s we need stable reason_code taxonomy. Please keep it small + documented; we’ll map to headers and error payload. Recommend separating QUOTA_EXCEEDED vs OVERLOAD_GUARDRAIL clearly.

2025-12-11 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Security note: decision logs must not be accessible broadly. Ensure log queries are behind the internal admin role and are audited. No tenant identifiers in metrics labels.

2025-12-13 (Jordan Lee): Implementing as pre-compiled lookup tables per route_group + tier + region. Added stable rule ordering by rule_id to enforce determinism. Adding decision_id derived from (request_id, policy_version, route_id) via SHA-256 -> UUIDv5.

2025-12-16 (Jordan Lee): PR opened: redwood#27418. Added policy lint rules: missing default for protected route group, conflicting overrides, and invalid enum values. Added evaluator micro-bench: p99 ~1.4ms with logs sampled at 1% (enterprise THROTTLE/SHED always logged).
2025-12-17 (Aisha Bello): Reviewed bench numbers—good. Please add metric for policy_eval_error_total and policy_eval_latency_ms (histogram) aggregated by route_id + priority_class + region.

2025-12-18 (Jordan Lee): Addressed feedback. Metrics added with bounded labels. Logging now redacts account_id in log payload; only input_fingerprint is included. Added docstring + examples for reason codes.

2025-12-19 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Security review sign-off pending: confirm decision logs don’t include tenant identifiers. input_fingerprint hash is ok. Ensure debug/explain endpoint is not part of this PR (keep separate).

2025-12-20 (Jordan Lee): Updated PR: removed any raw account identifiers from log payload; logs can be joined to request_id in internal tracing system. Added explicit access control note in README. Security sign-off received from Kaitlyn.
2026-01-07 (Jordan Lee): Merged PR-27418. Rolled out behind feature flag (ENG-4928). Routing team unblocked to consume priority_class + budgets in admission control path (ENG-4924).

2026-01-14 (Rafael Mendes): During canary game day, decision logs were used successfully to explain enterprise allows vs best-effort throttles. No determinism issues observed. Follow-up: ensure we retain logs long enough for enterprise escalations (tracked in ENG-4930/observability retention).
